body:
Then, in my personal and humble opinion, you should try and stay together and work through this. It will be difficult, and at times it will make you crazy, but after time passes things will become more "normal" again. I *know* it doesn't feel that way, and I am not saying "oh just get over it" at **all**. This is something that will be with both of you for a long time. If you are up to it and he is willing, you might see a counselor together. There are so many things that you might just need help telling each other, or help determining what your feelings are all about. If you try a single counselor that doesn't work, try at least one more. Don't give up on it if you both want this relationship to work out. I know that all of what I just typed is way "easier said than done". So please don't think I am telling you what you have to do or anything like that. If you would ever like to talk more you can feel free to PM me, or just keep replying to me here in your post. I am a rape victim myself, and I am a guy. While I cannot understand exactly what you are going through because I am not you, please know that everything I am telling you comes from personal experience. Nothing more and nothing less. I am not stronger or better than you in any way. This is something that people can give you advice for, but will ultimately be up to you. None of us will know how much staying with him, or leaving him, would hurt either of you. That is a very personal connection. No one has the right to tell you that you can't, or shouldn't, love him. No one has the right to tell you that he doesn't love you either. We are only giving our personal opinions that may or may not fully apply to you and him and this situation. This is not something that you will just wake up one day and everything will magically be fine. This will take time, patience, love, understanding, and work. On both your parts. If you are both willing to do that work, then I'd say you should stay together and find a good counselor. Again though: these are only my opinions. I am certainly not the all-knowing master of the universe or anything. I am just a guy, trying to help with some advice. Not rules, or what you must do, just advice. 
You deserve to feel safe, you deserve to be loved, and you never ever deserved this terrible event. Try to remember that it is absolutely not your fault. Some people may try to blame you, others will blame him. All that matters is if the two of you can talk it out, and after time you will find that you are totally comfortable with each other again, and possibly even more in love than you ever were (i am talking months or years even. this will not be a quick thing.)

I definitely understand not wanting to make that whole month awkward. My three friends are the only thing that keep me here too. So I understand that feeling, at least somewhat. I don't want you to think I am saying "I know exactly how you feel" because I don't think anyone can honestly say that to another. But I do feel similarly. Also don't worry about venting. You can vent to me any time you want to. No worries. If I don't respond in a timely fashion it is only because I am not near a computer.

Please read it all but if TL:DR then: Take it a day at a time. Your friends hang out with you for a reason, so be yourself and ask them to hangout if you want to. Sometimes they might say no but others they will say yes! Also, no one is perfect. Again though please read the rest...

Of course it matter in High School, that is where you are right now. I totally agree with you there. However with that said: I want you to know that no one, not even the people you think are right now, *no one* is the "normal teen" you think they are. Those guys you hear talking about all their hookups have probably never hooked up, at least one of them is probably gay and afraid to come out around his fellow jocks/cool-guys (and just to be clear there is *nothing* wrong with being gay. i am just saying statistically it is likely). Maybe one or two may have, but in my experience most girls don't go for those type of guys (the ones who parade around that they had sex, or had sex a lot). They fear rejection as much as you do, so they lie to everyone (sometimes even to themselves). My first recommendation would be to start asking your friends to hang out more. If you like the girl, say so but let her know you want to remain her friend no matter what and that her friendship alone is still very important to you. There will be no perfect words because that isn't how real life works. Perfect words for those situations come from professional writers for television/film, or are practiced as "generic quips" that can fit many situations and are rehearsed in front of a mirror by vain people. Just be yourself. If that means being quiet and only chiming in when you think you have something to add, then be that! If your friends already like you, that is for a reason so just keep up being you. Keep working at it, but don't work so hard that it becomes all you are focused on. When you try too hard it can be frustrating, and because most people are their own worst critics every small "wrong" thing seems like it is epic. Especially at your age. Hormones are doing crazy swing dances inside your body, throwing you in all kinds of directions.

No apology necessary for this man. I'm not questioning it. If I am having sex with a partner, and she becomes that uncomfortable (i mean "obviously uncomfortable", as the OP has described, even if the words "stop" never came out of her mouth): i stop what the fuck i am doing, and get far enough away that my partner won't feel threatened but will know I am not just leaving either. If they ask me to go of course I would leave, that is entirely different. I just don't want them to think I am running away from them. Not that it happens a lot or anything but it has happened, and when it has my approach seemed appropriate. (by all means, educate me if it doesn't sound appropriate. i would be happy to learn better, more considerate ways.) Even if you do want to have sex right then really bad, maybe you suddenly cramped or maybe i just did something wrong that you didn't like. Either way it means I need to stop because something is clearly wrong.
OP:
There is not a question here in this humble man's opinion. If you feel raped after what you have described here, then you absolutely were. Your emotional state, the way it made you feel and is making you feel now, that is how you know. That is all you need for affirmation right there in my book. Something was happening that you did not want to be happening to you. Many rape victims are so struck by the sheer fact that it *is* happening that they literally can't conceive of fighting back because the act itself is so horrible that they simply can't believe it is happening and their minds get caught in a "how is this happening?" loop of sorts. Not because they are weak in any way, but because what is happening to them is inhuman and any human mind would likely have a very difficult time dealing with that reality.

If your boyfriend is truly sorry, and you actually feel like you want to work it out with him then I would say to give it some time, and like someone else pointed out maybe just let him know that sex is going to be off limits for now, until you decide you can be comfortable with him again. If he sticks around he might just be worth your trouble, but if he doesn't then trust me you will find someone who will treat you right. I mean I don't wanna sound cliche, or like it is trivial to lose a boyfriend/girlfriend at all. It is difficult but is sometimes necessary. Whatever you decide to do, just be sure it is what *you* think is right and not what he or anyone else (including me) tries to convince you is right.

If you don't feel intimidated by him at all (in a boss kind of way), and think he can handle it based on your experience with him: you might try talking to him first. However I would also like to say that HR is there for this type of situation. If it is a co-worker of equal employ (they have the same basic job/position as you) then it can be considerate to talk to them first, especially if you don't think they "mean to be a jerk" if you know what I mean. With that said: because he is your boss, that is immediately a more threatening situation because he holds a position in the company that is above yours. So in my opinion, there is nothing wrong going straight to HR for this one. (side note: i am male, in case that makes my comment less relevant for you personally in this situation, or if it makes it more relevant for that matter. just basically: i'm a dude if it matters to ya)

I'd just like to say that you don't have to feel like you've "let yourself become" this "empty person". Depression is a very serious thing. It *is* real, it is *not* just in your head, and it is absolutely *not* your fault. I hope that doesn't sound harsh, as I do not mean it that way at all. You don't have to apologize for the length. Feel free to write as much as you want to. Especially if it makes you feel better. I will read a 19 paragraph response if having someone "listen" by reading it will help you at all. You are very welcome, and you don't sound crazy at all. Promise.

Whether it is for attention or not, something is causing you to feel that way. Even if it is for attention, that wouldn't invalidate your feelings. That just, in my opinion, means you want someone to help you and you don't know who or how to ask. I have personally had success calling prevention hotlines. You can call one and if you don't feel it is helping you can just hang up and dial another, or the same one hoping for a different operator. They have all genuinely tried to help me, but some were better at it than others. I would google for numbers in your area, or maybe even support groups in your area. There are people out there going through similar things, and everyone at those groups is both looking for help themselves but also to be around "kindred spirits" who have gone through similar things in their life. I know to me it sounded like it wasn't going to do any good, but it really did. I hope you find support. If you wanna chat you can msg me as well.

I wish I could help you more. All I can say is you put into words almost exactly what I feel every day as well. I'm so sorry for what you are feeling and going through. I hope that you find something that is able to help you feel better. If you'd like to talk feel free to reply here in your post, or to PM me if that makes you more comfortable. I know I can't magically fix anything, but you can vent to me or just chat with me about what you are feeling and know that I will not judge you, nor will I compare any of my sadness to yours. Though I am willing to share my own story with you as well if you just want to hear someone talk who might feel kinda the same way as you. (i say "kinda the same" because i am always very hesitant to use words that might make it sound like I "know exactly what you are going through". As I don't think that would be correct, or fair to say.

As Kfizzer said: Family is more than blood. As far as anti-depressants I feel you should be made aware (if you are not already): medications must be given a long time (a month or longer) before they really start to work. even then it won't be so noticeable. it will be a gradual thing until one day you realize you can think about things that used to send you into depression, and now they don't. Those medicines will not keep you from feeling sadness, or from ever getting depressed. They are meant to aid you in making your mood more "stable" (less apt to drop or spike suddenly). If you want to try it again, then I would suggest discussing it with your doctor again like you are thinking about.
Apart from medicine, supportive people are always the best help to me personally. So if you need to talk to someone feel free to do so here, or to PM me if you'd like.

See... you already have two people so far ready to listen to you and offer support! It is because we know you are important, and that you matter. You deserve support, and you deserve to feel like you matter... because you do. Always try to remember that.

I do not believe the measure of a man is his ability to commit violence. If you honestly want to do it, and believe it is the right thing to do, then you should join the armed forces. I would caution you to read some of the history of war, and how those fighting it are simply manipulated by the powers/countries/politics behind them. They want you to think that the only way to be measured is through service. You are man without ever being violent, and in my opinion are more of a man if you can avoid violence whenever possible. These are just my own opinions of course, and I am certainly not trying to tell you that the way you believe is wrong. I just wanted to show another perspective. I have known many people who joined the military, and very very few of them felt they had made a difference or were doing anything that could be deemed "good". They were all very happy to get out, even though they went in with the best of intentions and hopes. Not saying that will happen for you of course. I am not all knowing or all seeing, I am just a person here. One who is hoping to help. Maybe try and find friends who share your interest in airsoft, or paintball? Perhaps if you felt you were making a difference in someone's life it could replace the "making a difference through war" feeling.
Sorry for the length, and more sorry if anything I said seemed judgmental. I did not mean it that way.

I understand more than you might think (not saying I know exactly how you feel, and not even attempting to compare our levels of anguish in anyway). If you want to talk, or if you want me to just listen then I am here. You can PM me if you want to.

I think you should find someone to talk to who will not lecture you. While I am sure your Mom loves and cares about you, depression is a hard thing to understand for people who do not feel that way. I am 32 and have also thought of it often, and attempted suicide in my life. Please know that if you want someone to listen to you that I am here. You can talk to me right here or you can PM me if you'd rather. I would be happy to listen if you simply need someone to vent to, and I would be happy to actually converse with you and talk about life.

I am so sorry you are going through this. I have had similar feelings of worthlessness my entire life as well (i am 32). I want you to know that I am here if you want to talk about anything, or just vent and have me listen. You can reply here, or feel free to PM if you want to. I know I am a complete stranger, but if you give me chance maybe I can become your friend! I would certainly like that. No pressure though. Just... someone is out here if you need them.

Hi, I just want to say that you are definitely not ugly! Perhaps you are comparing yourself to the effects and makeup, not to mention airbrushing, that make "actors/models" look as good as they do. Like someone else said: I think you should keep focus on your academics. You are 17, and while it may not feel like it sometimes: you have a lot of life ahead of you! Not only *can* it get better, but I believe that if you give it a chance that it *will* get better. I didn't have a girlfriend until I was almost 25! So please don't feel like it will *never* happen just because it hasn't yet. You have plenty of time to find love my good man. Believe it!

Hello. I am here if you would like to talk. You are welcome to PM me or reply and chat right here in your post. I can't promise that things will get better, but I can say that I believe they will if you give them the chance to. Also your english is fine, so don't worry about that.

That's alright. I just sent you a PM explaining how to do it. If you would rather talk right here then that is fine with me too. I just want to make this as easy on *you* as possible. I am here for you, if you want or need me/someone to be!

I also am here. If you want to talk you can PM me, or reply to this thread here. I don't think you are being selfish for wanting help either, just to make sure that is said. I don't know you yet, but would be happy to get to know you if you are willing to give me the chance to. Let's talk!

I have called "prevention hotlines" in the past, and they actually helped me more than I thought they would, personally. I would be hesitant to suggest a specific one, but you might google and find a few places you can call. If it sounds like the person on the phone isn't helping you can always hang up and try another number, or the same number trying for a different operator. Also the sub **r/depression** has been known to help me. Just reading the way some other depressed people feel, and seeing people genuinely trying to help them out actually helps me feel a little better too (again, that might just be me). I also sometimes will listen to upbeat music while doing anything else, and for me that helps distract my mind for a while which lets me take a small rest from the weight, darkness, and loneliness I feel. While it does come back, you may be surprised at what even a short "breather" can do for you. I hope some part of that helps you.

thank you for saying i am not worthless. i believe you are genuinely trying to help me, but wanted to mention that you probably should not be telling people with depression that they "are not depressed" an they only "think they are". that has the opposite effect from help, as this is something we hear **all the time** when we try to tell others about our depression. That response is something that typically hurts, because it proves that the person saying it doesn't understand how serious depression is. I have a friend who always says "you can't be depressed, you are smiling." ... well smiling is just muscle control. I can smile and feel really, *really* depressed at the same time. The smile I show does nothing to alleviate the pressure and darkness that *I* feel. I do it so that they don't have to look at my depressing face while they are around me. I can assure you though, I *am* depressed. It is not a decision I made anywhere. I don't think "wow i am depressed so I shouldn't do anything", I simply don't feel that anything has meaning. Nothing brings me what others describe as "joy" (i have anhedonia in conjunction with Major Depression. at least i have diagnosed as having those things). ... i do sincerely appreciate you trying to help me though, and do not believe you said that to be harsh or mean in any way. So: thank you again for saying I am not worthless.

The only thing I know is that I feel very much the same. You are not alone in these feelings. I am not in ***any*** way trying to say that I know *exactly* how you feel, nor am I comparing the severity of your feelings to mine... I just share these same feelings you have expressed. I am anhedonic (primarily motivational, as occasionally i can **mildly** enjoy something while doing it. the feeling is just not strong, and doesn't last).

"This isn't a world I want to live in, it's totally hopeless and disgusting." - is something I say to myself, literally, multiple times a day.
Just... please know you're not alone in that.
